cars.generation: Fourth-generation EF Civic production-road performance-hatchback family
cars.variant: SiR E-EF9 five-speed manual — Japan August 1991 archive reference
cars.specification_market: Japan-market fourth-generation E-EF9 Civic SiR three-door, five-speed manual, using Honda’s archive explicitly dated August 1991. This is a dated selected specification, not a claim that the generation or SiR began in 1991: the generation was announced September 1987 and the VTEC SiR programme in September 1989. B16A, 1595 cc, 10.2 compression, 160 PS net at 7600 rpm and 15.5 kgm net at 7000 rpm. Original PS and kgm notation is retained without conversion to mechanical hp or Nm. The archive marks five-speed manual available and four-speed automatic unavailable for this SiR column; generic automatic boilerplate does not make this an automatic reference. Base SiR equipment is selected; viscous LSD was optional, not standard. No SiR II power steering/equipment, EG 170-PS engine, B16B Type R figures, competition tune or measured performance is copied.
cars.summary: The EF9 SiR brought Honda’s original high-revving DOHC VTEC concept to the Civic hatchback, pairing its 160-PS B16A with four-wheel double-wishbone suspension. It marks the Civic’s transition into the VTEC performance lineage before the later EG and Type R generations. Count this absent fourth-generation performance-road family once; SiR/SiR II grades, equipment packages, years and racing derivatives add no extra entries.

cars.generation: Second-generation DA/DB Integra production-road sporting family
cars.variant: XSi three-door, five-speed manual — April 1989 Japan launch reference
cars.specification_market: Japan April 1989 production launch, Integra XSi three-door coupe with five-speed manual. Original April 19 release announces three-door sales April 20, with the four-door following May 12; its net DOHC VTEC table gives 1595 cc, 160 PS at 7600 rpm and 15.5 kgm at 7000 rpm. The stated high-output condition is five-speed with premium unleaded fuel. Honda’s B16A retrospective explicitly labels its engine specification 1989 Integra XSi and supplies configuration, bore/stroke, compression and valvetrain. Native PS/kgm net values remain unconverted. Honda’s separately dated April 1993 XSi archive confirms the DA6 three-door identity but is not silently treated as an April 1989 production sheet. Its dimensions, weights, ratios and equipment are not imported. No four-door DA8 body, lower-spec ZC engine, automatic 150-PS calibration, later B16A evolution, US Acura B18 or DC2 Type R specification is copied.
cars.summary: The second-generation Integra launched Honda’s DOHC VTEC production-car era in April 1989. Its naturally aspirated 1.6-litre B16A used switchable valve timing and lift to combine high-rpm performance with everyday operation, a landmark that shaped later Honda sports engines. Count this absent Integra generation once across Honda/Acura identities, three-/four-door bodies and XSi/RSi grades; later years, transmissions and cosmetic treatments add no separate entries.
